key_insight: A mathematically equivalent re-implementation of PI-DeepONets removes redundant Branch-network evaluations, cutting tensor sizes and training cost without sacrificing accuracy.
engineering_relevance: This makes physics-informed operator learning more practical for higher-dimensional PDEs, including cases that would otherwise exceed GPU memory.
method: Restructure PI-DeepONet inputs so the Branch net is evaluated once per input function instead of repeatedly across collocation points.
Preserve the original physics-informed loss and operator form while reducing redundant tensor handling.
Analyze complexity and derive scaling laws for training time versus collocation points and input functions.
evidence_signal: Across 1D, 2D, and 3D linear advection tests, the modified model matched predictive accuracy while reducing training time, reaching up to 3.75× speed-up in 2D and enabling a 3D run on an NVIDIA A100 that the original could not fit in memory.
watch_item: The gain depends on implementation details and tensor layout, so performance improvements may vary with model size, dimensionality, and hardware memory limits.
paper_title: The importance of tensor handling and implementation of physics-informed DeepONets
